name: Poison Butterly
description:
# POISON BUTTERFLY

*Graceful and dreamy, the Poison Butterfly dispenses a venom that leads to instant death for corrupt and faithless hearts. A soul power within her, perhaps guided by ancient entities, invokes their presence and karmic justice.*

Death is not only a means of destruction or despair, but also a just retribution to restore balance and healthy karma. The ancient spirit that once possessed the Poison Butterfly used her to attract young, white, virgin sorceresses to take their lives in the enchanted forest, possessed by negative and hallucinatory entities. The contrast between her apparent grace and her role as a bringer of death, combined with the revelation of her past possession, creates an ambiguous and fascinating image of this mythical figure. Death, in her context, takes on a broader meaning, linked to purification and the restoration of cosmic order.

name: Emperor Scorpion
description:
Emperor Scorpions (*Pandinus imperator*) are among the largest and most iconic scorpions in the world. Native to West Africa, they can grow up to 8 inches long and are known for their glossy black exoskeleton and powerful pincers. Despite their intimidating appearance, emperor scorpions are relatively docile and use their pincers more than their mild venom to subdue prey.

They thrive in humid environments like tropical forests and burrows, feeding on insects, spiders, and small vertebrates. Their nocturnal habits and sensitivity to vibrations make them stealthy hunters. In captivity, they’re popular among enthusiasts due to their manageable temperament and striking look.

While their sting is comparable to a bee’s, emperor scorpions play a vital ecological role and are studied for their fluorescent properties under UV light. Their blend of size, strength, and gentleness makes them a fascinating ambassador of the Scorpiones order.

name: Hippopotame sur pastèque géante
description:
Un petit hippopotame cartoon en équilibre sur une pastèque géante.

Cette sculpture 3D stylisée joue sur l’humour, les couleurs vives et l’exagération des formes, avec un travail particulier sur les volumes organiques, la modélisation stylisée et les textures handpainted pour un rendu à la fois fun et expressif.

L’idée est née d’un mélange simple et joyeux : en ce moment, ma fille adore les hippopotames, manger des pastèques et surtout regarder des vidéos d’hippos en train de croquer dedans.

Le contraste entre le côté massif de l’animal et la légèreté de la situation crée une image proche de l’univers du cartoon 3D et du character design stylisé.

C’est un modèle léger, coloré et ludique, pensé comme une pièce de portfolio autour de la sculpture numérique, du texturing peint à la main et de l’illustration 3D, qui explore les codes du jeu vidéo stylisé et de l’animation cartoon.

Glass octopus 
study of transparency of materials

(Vitreledonella richardi) is a unique representative of deep-sea or bottom octopuses, the only species in the Vitreledonellidae family.

Some features:

Appearance: the body is almost transparent, with the exception of some internal organs.

Size: mantle - up to 11 cm, total body length - up to 45 cm, weight - up to 450 grams. 14

Tentacles: the upper three pairs are quite long and almost equal to each other, the fourth pair is almost twice as short.

Suckers: small, located in one row (usually in three rows) and quite weak.

Eyes: located on long thin legs, widely spaced and always directed upwards.

Habitat: found almost everywhere in tropical and subtropical waters with a relatively deep bottom (about 100 meters and deeper).

name: Emperor penguin egg
description:
The emperor penguin,* Aptenodytes forsteri Gray*, 1844, is the largest and tallest Antarctic penguin.
The emperor penguin is the only penguin that rear its eggs during the Antarctic winter. These are incubated on males feet and kept warm thanks to the presence of a special brood pouch made by a flap of warm skin in the penguin belly. Thanks to this flap, eggs can be kept warm and safe even when outside temperature is -60 degrees °C. This egg is one of the several unhatched eggs that can be found in a penguin rookery ate the beginning of the Austral spring. an measure about 11 cm in lenght. This egg was collected in Cape Washington, one of the largest emperor penguin rookeries in the Ross Sea.

The chick specimen can be seen [in this model](http://sketchfab.com/3d-models/emperor-penguin-chick-d12698e168b94abf8368ba9e4427ee77).

This 3D model was realized by Clarissa Bignoli and Erika Del Bene during the Universal Civil Service (SCU) at UniGe.

name: Etruscan seal (right cuboid)
description:
3D scan of the right cuboid of the Etruscan seal (*Pliophoca etrusca*).

The fossil skeleton of *Pliophoca etrusca*, collected in1900 by Antonio di Paco from the upper Pliocene (Piacenzian) clays of Casa Nuova locality, near Orciano Pisano (Tuscany, Pisa province, Italy) is the best preserved and most complete fossil seal of the northern hemysphere and holotype of the fossil species *Pliophoca etrusca*.
This specimen was first described in detail and referred to the extant Mediterranean monk seal *Monachus albiventer* (=*Monachus monachus*) by Ugolini (1902); later on Tavani (1941) redescribed this specimen and assigned it to the new genus and species of monachine seals *Pliophoca etrusca*. It was finally redescribed by Berta et al. (2015).

Specimen: *Pliophoca etrusca* Tavani, 1941

Inventory number: I13993

Collection: Natural History Museum University of Pisa

Find out more about the Museum at [https://www.msn.unipi.it/it/](http://)

name: Marrano de San Antón (La Alberca, Salamanca)
description:
Gemelo digital del marrano de San Antón (La Alberca, Salamanca)

En La Alberca (uno de los pueblos más bonitos de España), junto a su iglesia, se encuentra una curiosa escultura de piedra: el marrano de San Antón. 🐖 Su presencia está ligada a una tradición que ha perdurado durante siglos y que sigue viva hoy en día.

Según la tradición de San Antón, cada año, se libera un cerdo en las calles de La Alberca, que es alimentado por los vecinos hasta el 17 de enero, día de San Antón, patrón de los animales. En esa fecha, el cerdo es subastado, y los fondos recaudados se destinan a obras benéficas. Esta tradición simboliza la solidaridad y la cooperación entre los habitantes del pueblo, creando un fuerte lazo comunitario.

La escultura: Realizada en granito, fue colocada en su lugar en el año 1996, a modo de homenaje a una tradición de secular. Se ha convertido en todo un emblema del pueblo, atrayendo a curiosos y viajeros que quieren conocer de cerca esta costumbre tan especial.

name: Kirk's dik-dik
description:
3D scan of the right mandible of Kirk's dik-dik (*Madoqua kirkii*). 


Kirk's dik-dik is a species of small dik-dik antelope native to Eastern and Southern Africa.
Dik-diks are some of the world's smallest antelopes, and the Kirk's dik-dik is the largest, standing between 35 and 45 cm tall and weighing no more than 7.2 kg. It is sexually dimorphic; females are larger and lack horns, while males sport a more developed muzzle, have a longer crest, and tend to be lighter in colour. It lives in the savannah areas of eastern and southwestern Africa, it is nocturnal and has and herbivorous diet that consists mainly of foliage, fruits, shoots, and berries.


Specimen: Kirk's dik-dik  *Madoqua kirkii* (Günther, 1880)

name: Strumigenys liui sp. nov.
description:
*Strumigenys liui* sp. nov. – Hamer, Tang & Guénard 2025
This new species was found in the forested mountains of Yunnan Province, China.

Holotype (MCZ-ENT00759758) dataset consists of surface volume rendering image stacks of PNG files comprising full face views stills of the head, whole body in lateral and dorsal view, as well as dorsal view of postpetiole and first gastral tergites. Further, raw CT-scan data (nii format), and a full 3D surface model (STL format) are made available. Digital stacked colour images (tif format) of the head in full face view, and the whole body in dorsal and lateral view are also provided. All data is deposited on Zenodo (https://doi.org/10.5281/zenodo.14830376).

See the full study -  Hamer et al., 2025. ‘A review of the rare *Strumigenys mnemosyne* (Formicidae; Myrmicinae) group using micro-CT scanning, with the description of three new species, and the virtual repair of a broken paratype.’ DOI LINK will be provided upon publication.

name: Faun
description: Este proyecto consiste en la creación de una figurita de porcelana de una faun femenina, diseñada como un prop. El proceso comenzó con la creación de la versión high poly, enfocándose en los detalles finos del cuerpo, cabello y ropa, todo modelado en ZBrush. A continuación, se realizó el modelo low poly en Maya, manteniendo un balance entre detalle y optimización para asegurar un buen rendimiento. Se generaron las UVs en Maya para preparar la malla para el siguiente paso. Luego, se realizó la retopología para mejorar la distribución de polígonos y facilitar el baking de mapas como normales, AO y otros detalles en Marmoset Toolbag. Finalmente, las texturas fueron creadas en Substance Painter, utilizando técnicas de pintura detallada y enmascarado para replicar la apariencia de la porcelana y los textiles, logrando un acabado realista y de alta calidad para la figurita.

name: BIOARQUITECTURA 1 CORTE
description:
Modelos elaborados en el marco del trabajo de grado ***“Mundos plausibles y bioarquitecturas: Modelos de simulación para la coevolución entre sistemas ecológicos habitables”***, desarrollado como requisito para optar al título de Arquitecta en la Pontificia Universidad Javeriana, Facultad de Arquitectura y Diseño.

Estas bioarquitecturas fueron construidas en el entorno del *videojuego Minecraft y exportadas mediante la herramienta Mineways*, como parte de una metodología de simulación computacional orientada a explorar configuraciones espaciales adaptativas, ecosistémicamente sensibles y plausibles desde una perspectiva biocéntrica. Los modelos se utilizaron en procesos de simulación bioarquitectónica aplicados a mundos posibles, y forman parte del componente experimental de la investigación. Para conocer en profundidad la propuesta y su desarrollo, la tesis completa se encuentra disponible en el repositorio de la universidad.

name: Brazilian Wandering Spider
description:
**Brazilian Wandering Spider (Phoneutria spp.)**
   - Highly venomous, aggressive.
   - Known for hiding in banana shipments.

**The Brazilian Wandering Spider (*Phoneutria* spp.) is one of the most venomous spiders in the world**, earning its reputation through potent neurotoxic venom and aggressive behavior. Native to tropical South America, especially Brazil, it belongs to the family Ctenidae and includes species like *Phoneutria nigriventer* and *P. fera*.

Unlike web-building spiders, it roams at night in search of prey, using its speed and strength to ambush insects and small vertebrates. Its bite can cause intense pain, muscle spasms, and in rare cases, serious medical complications, though antivenom has greatly reduced fatalities.

The nickname “banana spider” stems from its occasional presence in banana shipments, sparking fear and fascination worldwide. Despite its notoriety, the Brazilian Wandering Spider plays a vital ecological role and studied for its venom’s potential in medical research.

name: Shortfin mako shark
description:
Найшвидша акула у світі: Короткоперий мако (Isurus oxyrinchus) вважається найшвидшою акулою в океані, здатною розвивати швидкість до 74 км/год у коротких ривках, що робить її грозою для швидкої здобичі, як-от тунця.
Теплокровність: На відміну від більшості акул, короткоперий мако частково теплокровний завдяки спеціальній системі кровообігу, що дозволяє підтримувати температуру тіла на 4-5 °C вище за температуру води, підвищуючи її активність.
Стрибки над водою: Ця акула відома своєю здатністю вистрибувати з води на висоту до 6 метрів під час полювання або коли її зачепили на гачок, що робить її популярною серед рибалок-спортсменів.
Харчування: Короткоперий мако — хижак вершини харчового ланцюга. Вона полює на швидких риб (тунця, меч-рибу), кальмарів, а великі особини можуть нападати навіть на дельфінів та інших акул.
Розмір і тривалість життя: Дорослі особини зазвичай досягають 2,5-3,2 метра в довжину, хоча найбільші можуть сягати 4,5 метра і важити до 600 кг.

The fossil skeleton of *Pliophoca etrusca*, collected in1900 by Antonio di Paco from the upper Pliocene (Piacenzian) clays of Casa Nuova locality, near Orciano Pisano (Tuscany, Pisa province, Italy) is the best preserved and most complete fossil seal of the northern hemysphere and holotype of the fossil species *Pliophoca etrusca*.
This specimen was first described in detail and referred to the extant Mediterranean monk seal *Monachus albiventer* (=*Monachus monachus*) by Ugolini (1902); later on Tavani (1941) redescribed this specimen and assigned it to the new genus and species of monachine seals *Pliophoca etrusca*. It was finally redescribed by Berta et al. (2015).

name: Ember-tailed Burrower - Australia
description:
The Ember-Tailed Burrower (Pyrocaudus terranovae) is a subterranean marsupial found in Australia’s arid interior. Roughly the size of a rabbit, it has powerful forelimbs with curved claws for digging complex burrow systems. Its most distinctive feature is its fiery-orange, bioluminescent tail, which researchers believe may serve as a communication tool in dark tunnels.

Covered in coarse, sand-colored fur, the Ember-Tailed Burrower blends seamlessly into its desert surroundings. Its small, sensitive eyes indicate a reliance on touch and smell over vision. Feeding on roots, tubers, and small invertebrates, it plays a key role in soil aeration.

Discovered only in the late 19th century, P. terranovae remains elusive, emerging mainly at dusk. Conservationists are monitoring populations as habitat loss threatens this fascinating, glow-tailed digger.

name: Benin Bronze Ram
description:
This bronze sculpture of a ram, dating between the 15th and 19th centuries, originates from the Kingdom of Benin, in present-day Nigeria. It features a naturalistic, muscular form with finely incised surface textures that mimic the animal’s fur. The ram stands alert, its head slightly raised, and a single, sweeping horn curves elegantly along its neck—a hallmark of the sculptor’s craftsmanship.

Unlike similar ram figures such as the aquamanile in the British Museum—used as ceremonial ewers with functional openings—this piece lacks spouts or perforations, indicating it was not designed to hold liquid. Instead, it likely served a symbolic purpose, possibly placed on a royal altar as an emblem of kingship and authority.

In Benin cosmology, the ram embodies masculinity and perseverance, and was ritually sacrificed during the Ague Ceremony, an important royal festival instituted by Oba Esigie in the 16th century.

name: Solar Veilfish - fish
description:
Solar Veilfish (Aurelolamina pelagia)

Discovered in 2022 by marine biologist Dr. Hana Mori near the Azores, the Solar Veilfish inhabits open-ocean depths of 100–500 meters. This sleek predator glides effortlessly, its scale-less, iridescent skin shifting between silver and deep blue to blend with the shimmering waves above. Its ribbon-like fins emit faint bioelectric pulses, possibly for communication or stunning prey. With retractable fangs and lightning-fast reflexes, it ambushes small squid and fish, thriving in the twilight zone of the ocean.

name: Final Exam Witch House Project
description: Deep within a colorful, ever-shifting magical forest stands a crooked little witch house that seems to belong there and not at the same time, as if it chose the spot on a whim and the forest simply agreed. A lone witch lives inside, quietly tending to the woods through small spells and bubbling potions brewed in the cauldron beside her door, where magic has seeped into the grass and turned it warm and golden. Her broom rests nearby, always ready, while the forest subtly hides the house from those who wander in with unkind intentions, revealing it only to the curious or the lost. Though the witch keeps to herself, her presence keeps the forest balanced, vibrant, and gently enchanted, making the house a small but vital heartbeat in the deep, magical woods.
tags: forest, Magical, witchhouse, magicforest, witch, magicalforest

The sculpted feathers form an ornate, almost baroque relief, while the long, curved beak and slender, clawed feet give it a look that is both refined and unsettling. Perfect for fans of dark, sophisticated atmospheres, this model fits seamlessly into artistic worlds that merge melancholy with visual flair. name: Etruscan seal (right capitatum)
description:
3D scan of the right capitatum of the Etruscan seal (*Pliophoca etrusca*).

The fossil skeleton of *Pliophoca etrusca*, collected in1900 by Antonio di Paco from the upper Pliocene (Piacenzian) clays of Casa Nuova locality, near Orciano Pisano (Tuscany, Pisa province, Italy) is the best preserved and most complete fossil seal of the northern hemysphere and holotype of the fossil species *Pliophoca etrusca*.
This specimen was first described in detail and referred to the extant Mediterranean monk seal *Monachus albiventer* (=*Monachus monachus*) by Ugolini (1902); later on Tavani (1941) redescribed this specimen and assigned it to the new genus and species of monachine seals *Pliophoca etrusca*. It was finally redescribed by Berta et al. (2015).

Specimen: *Pliophoca etrusca* Tavani, 1941

Inventory number: I13993

Collection: Natural History Museum University of Pisa

Find out more about the Museum at [https://www.msn.unipi.it/it/](http://)

Scanned and edited by Chiara Sorbini

Scanner: Artec spider
designer_displayName: Natural History Museum, University of Pisa

name: Hyoid bone of a howler monkey
description:
3D scan of a hyoid bone of a howler monkey (*Alouatta* sp.). 

Howler monkeys are known for their howls/roars. They are able to create such loud and specific sounds by specific body shape and structures. The larynx is enlarged and they have an enlarged open chest that creates a resonating chamber to increase the sound produced. The howlers also have specialized vocal chords to produce the specific sound and the hyoid bone, a horseshoe-shaped bone, is extra-large to allow them to howler.

Specimen: howler monkey, Alouatta sp.

Inventory number: C 3173

Collection: Natural History Museum University of Pisa 

Find out more about the Museum at https://www.msn.unipi.it/it/

Scanned and edited by Marco Merella

name: Giganotosaurus Carolinii (Pardus Skin Version)
description:
**NOTICE**
- There is a bug/issue with importing a rigged fbx mesh on Sketchfab at the moment, causing odd displacement of the mesh (most noticeable on the teeth and spikes) which the original mesh does not have. 
- The weird glitching movements in some animations are caused by some Bbone unexportable from Blender.

Being one of the **BIG THREE** largest theropods, the **Giganotosaurus** surely lives up to its name. Though reconstructed as jagged, spiky, and crocodilian-like in a certain movie franchise, here the creature is reconstructed with accurate anatomy and musculature in mind, alongside 3 uniquely designed skins that give the animal 3 distinct yet plausible looks.

The 3D model is Production-Ready, featuring the **new version 3.0 Rig Type**, which includes advanced rig controls, muscle-like movements and deformation, added new precise controls, FK & IK bones, stretch bones and jiggle bones, with added new corrective joints, and with the custom Rig UI N-panel.

The aye-aye is a long-fingered lemur native to Madagascar with rodent-like teeth that perpetually grow and a special thin middle finger. It is the world's largest nocturnal primate.  The species has an average head and body length of 36–43 cm plus a tail of 56–61 cm. The aye-aye is an omnivore and commonly eats seeds, nuts, fruits, nectar, plant exudates and fungi.

name: Fossil brown bear (right radius)
description:
3D scan of the right radius of a  fossil brown bear (*Ursus arctos*). 


Fossil of a prime adult female skull of brown bear. The specimen was found in "Abisso Oriano Coltelli" cave (44°05'35,0 N, 10°14'47,0" E, labelled T/Lu 642 in the Tuscan register of caves) which opens at 1209 m a.s.l on the western slope of "Monte Alto di Sella" (Apuan Alps). The mammal assemblage collected consists of 486 investigated specimens, 127 of which belong to an individual skeleton of brown bear. The bear died from non-violent causes, probably during hibernation. The specimen was dated providing a conventional age of 6480 ± 40 14 C ka BP (Holocene).
More information : https://amq.aiqua.it/index.php/amq/article/view/112


Specimen: Brown bear, *Ursus arctos* Linnaeus, 1758

Inventory number: I17771

Collection: Natural History Museum University of Pisa 

Find out more about the Museum at https://www.msn.unipi.it/it/

Scanned and edited by Luca Pandolfi

name: West indian manatee (scale model)
description:
3D scan of the scale model (22 cm) of a West Indian manatee (*Trichechus manatus*). 

This resin model was created by [Naturaliter Srl](https://www.naturaliter.com/) for the exhibition Not Only Cetaceans. Complementing the exhibition dedicated to marine mammals, this display focuses on animals that have adapted to life in the water through evolutionary pathways different from those of dolphins and whales. The exhibition features sirenians (dugongs and manatees), pinnipeds (sea lions, seals, and walruses), and the polar bear. On display are complete skeletons and skulls from the Museum’s historical collections, as well as scale and life-size models and casts of both extant and extinct species. The scale models were specifically designed to be tactile, enabling visually impaired and blind people, to explore and understand the shapes of these animals and their fossil ancestors.

Specimen: West Indian manatee, *Trichechus manatus* Linnaeus, 1758

Scanned and edited by Simone Farina

name: Animated Carnotaurus
description:
This scientifically accurate 3D model of Carnotaurus has been created by closely following fossil evidence and modern paleontological research. The body proportions, skeletal structure, and muscle anatomy are carefully reconstructed to reflect the real animal as accurately as possible. The skull features its characteristic short, deep shape with correctly positioned and sized horns, while the jaw structure conveys the powerful bite mechanics of this theropod. The extremely reduced forelimbs are modeled to match their limited mobility, and the strong, well-balanced tail highlights Carnotaurus’s ability to run at high speeds. Skin details are based on current scientific assumptions, featuring realistic scale patterns, natural folds, and subtle asymmetry, giving the model a lifelike presence suitable for high-quality renders, animation, and educational purposes.

name: Animated Carchradontosaurus
description:
This 3D model represents Carcharodontosaurus, one of the largest known theropod dinosaurs that lived during the mid-Cretaceous period (~100–94 million years ago) in North Africa.

The anatomy is based on current paleontological research, incorporating accurate skeletal proportions, muscle mass reconstruction, and posture consistent with large carcharodontosaurid theropods. The elongated skull features sharp, blade-like teeth adapted for slicing flesh,

Surface details include realistic skin folds, scale variation, and asymmetry to reflect a living animal rather than a stylized creature. The body proportions emphasize powerful hind limbs for locomotion, a heavy counterbalancing tail, and reduced but muscular forelimbs.

This model is suitable for scientific visualization, documentaries, educational projects, and high-end realistic renders.

name: Hoazinoides
description:
Step back into the ancient tropical forests of the Middle Miocene with this scientifically inspired 3D model of Hoazinoides (Hoazinoides magdalenensis).

Discovered in the famous fossil-rich La Venta deposits of Colombia, Hoazinoides is a captivating piece of avian evolutionary history. Living approximately 13 to 11 million years ago, this extinct prehistoric bird is an ancient relative of the bizarre modern-day Hoatzin (often known as the "stinkbird" or "reptile bird" of the Amazon).

name: Capra ibex #16118
description:
The Alpine ibex (Capra ibex), also known as the steinbock, is a European species of goat which lives in the Alps. It is one of ten species in the genus Capra and its closest living relative is the Iberian ibex. The Alpine ibex is a sexually dimorphic species; males are larger and carry longer horns than females. Its coat is brownish-grey. Alpine ibexes tend to live in steep, rough terrain and open alpine meadows. They can be found at elevations as high as 3,300 m (10,800 ft) and their sharp hooves allow them to scale the steep slopes and cliffs of their mountainous habitat.

This model was realized by Glenda Cantale during the Universal Civil Service (SCU) at the Genoa University.

3D scan of the skull of a juvenile scimitar oryx (*Oryx dammah*) 


The scimitar oryx is a species that was once widespread across North Africa and parts of West Africa and Central Africa. It is adapted to harsh desert conditions and can survive for months or even years without drinking water. A grazing animal, it derives most of its daily moisture intake from plants.
The head and body measures  is 140–240 cm; the tail is 45–60 cm long and ends with a tuft. Both male and female oryxes have horns, with the females' being more slender. The horns are long, thin, and symmetrical, and curve backward (a distinctive feature of this species).



Specimen: Scimitar oryx, *Oryx dammah* (Cretzschmar, 1826)

Inventory number: C 1278

Collection: Natural History Museum University of Pisa 

Find out more about the Museum at https://www.msn.unipi.it/it/

name: Taco xilográfico de la Puerta Sol
description:
La xilografía a testa, también llamada a contrafibra, es una técnica de grabado en relieve donde la madera se corta perpendicular al tronco del árbol. Utilizando herramientas como buriles o gubias se talla la imagen deseada. El resultado es un relieve que se entinta y se imprime sobre papel. 

Este taco, realizado en madera de boj y conservado en la Imprenta Municipal de Madrid-Artes del libro, se utilizó para la impresión de la ilustración de la Puetrta del Sol de Madrid en el libro de Mesonero  Nuevo Manual de Madrid histórico-topográfico-estadístico y descriptivo de Madrid, 1854.

description:
**Mapa de distribución:** https://drive.google.com/uc?export=view&id=1EbN5sf37RPkJ6SM8mxy2F-AGcfPnhc3Z

**Taxonomía:**

Familia: Diodontidae.

Género: Diodon.

Nombre científico:* *Diodon holocanthus.**

Nombre común: Pez globo espinoso, Pez erizo.

**Categoría de riesgo:**

NOM-059-SEMARNAT-2010: Sujeto a protección especial.

IUCN: Preocupación Menor (Least Concern, LC).

CITES: No listado.

**Esqueleto:** cuerpo esférico cubierto de espinas eréctiles que utiliza como mecanismo de defensa al inflarse cuando se siente amenazado.

**Dato curioso:** cuando se infla, puede alcanzar hasta el doble de su tamaño normal y sus espinas se erigen, lo que lo convierte en un objetivo difícil para los depredadores. Además, contiene una toxina extremadamente potente, la tetrodotoxina, que es mortal incluso en pequeñas dosis.

name: Humboldt's white-fronted capuchin
description:
3D scan of the skeleton of Humboldt's white-fronted capuchin (*Cebus albifrons*). 

The Humboldt's white-fronted capuchin is a species of gracile capuchin monkey that lives in primary forest but also in various types of secondary forest in Colombia, Venezuela, Brazil, and potentially the island of Trinidad. The head and body length is about 37.5 cm and the tail length for males is about 42.5 cm and it is between 41 and 46 cm for females. Its diet is varied, including fruits, leaves, nuts, seeds, insects, other invertebrates, and small vertebrates.

Specimen: Humboldt's white-fronted capuchin, Cebus albiforns (Humboldt, 1812)

Inventory number: C 1742

Collection: Natural History Museum University of Pisa
 
Find out more about the Museum at https://www.msn.unipi.it/it/

Scanned and edited by Marco Merella and Simone Farina

This animal is the African wild dog (Lycaon pictus)
Dog 3d model Free
The scientific name, Lycaon pictus, literally translates to "painted wolf," referring to its unique, mottled coat. No two dogs have the same coat pattern, making these markings as unique as a human fingerprint. Distinctive physical features include its large, rounded ears and a bushy tail that typically has a white tip

name: Inner longitudinal muscle of a pangolin tongue
description: 3D muscle architecture of a portion of the tongue of a white-bellied pangolin (Phataginus tricuspis). Using Iodine-contrast microCT, we applied an AI-assisted fiber tracking algorithm to visualize and reconstruct the muscle fascicles of the different muscles of the tongue. Pangolin tongues act as modified muscular hydrostats, with layers of outer muscles contracting to squeeze the elongated mobile tongue out of the pangolin's body. A central pair of retractor muscles help pull the tongue back in. These muscles are anchored to a pair of elongated xiphisternal bones that coil within the right flank of the animal. Thanks to Brookfield Zoo. https://doi.org/10.1093/icb/icaf049. Zobek et al., 2025. 3D Muscle Architecture of the Tongue of the White-bellied Pangolin (Phataginus tricuspis) Reveals a Muscular Hydrostat. Integrative and Comparative Biology

name: Dientes de Sable
description:
El término «dientes de sable» es un término genérico que se usa para describir a numerosas especies de mamíferos dotados de enormes caninos que vivieron durante diferentes épocas del Cenozoico.

Estas especies adquirieron sus característicos dientes de sable de forma totalmente independiente. La morfología de los dientes se puede considerar como ejemplo de evolución convergente, ya que ha ocurrido repetida e independientemente en al menos cuatro grupos diferentes de mamíferos: los macairodontes (Machairodontinae), una subfamilia de los félidos que incluye al famoso Smilodon; los nimrávidos (Nimravidae), una familia emparentada con los felinos, pero diferente; y finalmente, un par de casos aislados dentro de los creodontos (que no son considerados carnívoros auténticos) y los tilacosmílidos, una familia extinta de metaterios sudamericanos.

name: Giraffe
description:
3D scan of the skeleton of a giraffe (*Giraffa camelopardalis*). 

The giraffe is a large African hoofed mammal, and it is the tallest living terrestrial animal and the largest ruminant on Earth. Its scattered range extends from Chad in the north to South Africa in the south, and from Niger in the west to Somalia in the east. It usually inhabits savannahs and woodlands where it feeds on leaves, fruits, and flowers of woody plants, primarily acacia species.
The giraffe stands from 4.3 to 5.7 m tall, with males taller than females. The average weight is 1,192 kg for an adult male and 828 kg for an adult female.




Specimen: Giraffe, *Giraffa camelopardalis* (Linnaeus, 1758)

name: Portunidae
description:
Portunidae, Tristan de Cunha, Icefish 2004

Portunidae is the family of brachiopod decapod crustaceans that includes many genera of swimming crabs: they are characterized by the fifth pair of thoracic limbs, which have flattened, widened, paddle-shaped segments, thus facilitating swimming and floating. 
The ICEFISH expedition generated extensive large-scale benthic and geological datasets, significantly improving our understanding of the biogeographic provinces and island shelf areas of the surveyed regions. The ICEFISH cruise track illustrates the wide range of water masses and frontal systems that were sampled. The Burdwood Banks, the Falkland Islands/Islas Malvinas, and Tristan da Cunha lie outside the Antarctic Polar Front (APF), whereas the remaining islands are located within this front.

This 3D model was realized by Clarissa Bignoli and Erika Del Bene during the Universal Civil Service (SCU) at UniGe.

name: Pferdemodell
description:
Dieses 3D-Modell repräsentiert ein historisches Pferdemodell aus der Sammlung der Kunst- und Naturalienkammer der Franckeschen Stiftungen. Es wurde erstellt, um als Lehrmittel für den Schulunterricht im 18. Jahrhundert zu dienen. Dieses Modell vermittelt verschiedene Themen rund um das Pferd, darunter verschiedene Pferderassen, Pflegepraktiken, Krankheiten.

Das Pferd wird als Reitpferd präsentiert und ist mit einem deutschen Sattel ausgestattet. Zusätzlich wird es mit einem Brustschmuck und einem Gurt gezeigt, welches das Pferd als Zugpferd für leichte Kutschen ausweist.

Dieses Modell bietet die Möglichkeit, historische Aspekte der Pferdehaltung zu erforschen und ein tieferes Verständnis für die Arbeit verschiedener Berufsgruppen zu entwickeln, die eng mit Pferden verbunden waren.

name: Acrocanthosaurus
description: Acrocanthosaurus was a formidable theropod dinosaur that lived during the Early Cretaceous period, approximately 113 to 110 million years ago. Known for its impressive size and distinct features, this carnivorous dinosaur could reach lengths of up to 40 feet and weigh around 6 tons. One of the most striking characteristics of Acrocanthosaurus was the series of tall neural spines on its vertebrae, creating a pronounced ridge along its back and neck, which may have supported a muscular hump or sail. With a powerful jaw filled with sharp teeth, strong hind limbs, and clawed hands, Acrocanthosaurus was a top predator in its ecosystem, preying on large herbivorous dinosaurs. Its fossils have been predominantly found in North America, providing significant insights into the diversity and adaptability of large theropods during the Cretaceous.
